To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the relative cumulation of BHC isomers is different from that of DDT, and that 6‐BCH has a higher relative cumulative potential in the food chain than the other isomers.
6‐BCH is the most toxic and persistent isomer of BHC, which accumulates in the environment and in the food chain.
the β‐BHC isomer is more persistent and more toxic than α‐BHC and the γ‐BHC isomers are the least persistent and the least toxic.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
β‐BHC is the only isomer that has a high potential for bioaccumulation in the food chain.
the β‐isomer is the most persistent in the food chain, followed by α‐, γ‐, and ‐ δ‐BHC.
the relative accumulation of 6‐ and 2‐BHC in the food chain is not a general phenomenon, but depends on the type of the food chain and the environmental factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ecological relations of the individual BHC‐isomers are different and the results of the model experiment confirm the conclusions of the field study.
the ecological and biological studies have demonstrated a higher relative cumulability of 6‐ and α‐BHC than of the other isomers.
β‐, α, and δ‐BHC are the most persistent isomers of BCH in the ecological system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
6‐BCH is a persistent compound, and the relative cumulation of β‐BHC in food of animal origin should be taken into account in the evaluation of human exposure.
